author: Geoff Shackelford
title: Major(s) News & Notes January 29, 2026
text:
Major(s) News & Notes January 29, 2026
Koepka returns while Reed says goodbye to LIV. Plus, CBS outlines 2026 plans, Masters odds highlight prediction market issues, DCP takes on the Aimpointers, This, That, Quotables, and Reads.
Days to the Masters Honorary Starters Ceremony: 70
Days to the Chevron Championship first round: 84
Days to the PGA Championship first round: 105
Days to the U.S. Women’s Open first round: 126
Days to the Curtis Cup opening session: 134
Days to the U.S. Open first round: 140
Days to the KPMG Women’s PGA first round: 147
Days to The Open first round: 168
Days to the AIG Women’s Open first round: 182
Days to the Walker Cup opening session: 219
Judging by the hype, you’d think Brooks Koepka had been hit by a Greyhound bus, transported to Area 51 to have his limbs removed, only to have them reattached in a Netflix live-streamed surgery by Dr. Neal El Attrache.
The 35-year-old five-time major winner is merely returning to PGA Tour play after a brief three-year tour of some of the worst golf courses known to man. Koepka appeared early this week in La Jolla just as everyone remembered from seeing him at last year’s majors: looking like he’d just gotten out of bed and delivering clipped answers in a monotone flatter than a Rees Jones design.
Golf fans already knew the faux tough guy wouldn’t be crooning classics while backed by the Ponte Vedra Brass. The five-time major champion’s appeal comes from an innate ability to flip a switch at majors, a superpower that vanished after his 2023 PGA Championship win.
Koepka will eventually be joined on the PGA Tour by Patrick Reed, who announced he is returning for the 2027 season after an early check-out from the Four Aces hotel. But if anyone defines checking out but never leaving, Reed’s PGA Tour return won’t be celebrated, given the pathetic legal actions befitting a man of little character and taken during an ill-fated partnership with now-suspended lawyer Larry Klayman.
Unlike Koepka’s decision to return, the PGA Tour posted a tidy and hardly-celebratory story confirming Reed’s eligibility. He resigned his membership prior to “violating any regulations” and would be eligible to return to competition “on Aug. 25, 2026, as a non-member, provided that he complies with Tour regulations and does not participate in additional unauthorized events.”
Smart stipulations given that we’re dealing with PReed and his bonkers “team.”
This also means the former Farmers Insurance Open champion won’t get to pick up and improve his lies at Torrey Pines this week. Instead, he’s the top-ranked player at this week’s DP World Tour stop in Bahrain.
Continuing the PGA Tour trend of the first three weeks, this may also be the last time an event is played at Torrey Pines in January. SBJ’s Josh Carpenter reports that Torrey Pines might become a playoff stop. Since the San Diego city course is not on any org’s radar for future majors, a playoff event would at least be intriguing (weather and time zone-wise). But it would also be surprising to see the Tour wave the white flag on the pre-Super Bowl week date that’s been working well.
“This weekend between Championship weekend and the Super Bowl is pure gold when it comes to real estate in television,” Jim Nantz said in a CBS Sports call to preview the network’s 22-event run (more below). “As long as the NFL has an open weekend – and that could change moving forward with their schedule, I have no idea where that’s going – but this to me would be the No. 1 piece of real estate you can have on the West Coast for television.”
The Tour’s desire to abandon NFL weeks received mixed news, with Golf Channel reporting robust audiences for last week’s American Express won by Scottie Scheffler. Despite finishing against the AFC and NFC Championship games that averaged 48.1 and 46.8 million viewers, the four days of AmEx golf averaged 515,000 viewers on Golf Channel, while viewership tipped over a million on Saturday and even saw a 617,000 final round average audience, going primarily against the tight AFC game.
Less fortunate: the previous week’s final Sony Open, won by Chris Gotterup, only drew a pitiful 106,000 viewer final round average against thrilling NFL games.
In a surprising flex that could be seen as an ominous sign for Golf Channel’s current PGA Tour rights deal, ESPN has been allowed to air Thursday and Friday’s early round Farmers Insurance Open, once exclusively relegated to its ESPN+ streaming app. They will also be breaking protocol by streaming the coverage on Hulu and Disney+.
While Golf Channel will still have four hours each weekday afternoon and the early weekend coverage until CBS takes over, the move could signal that ESPN is interested in acquiring more golf. While ESPN is billing this as part of the special nature around Koepka’s return (along with a solid field that includes Mssrs. Aberg, Schauffele, Bradley, Rose and Matsuyama), they may have found a place for golf in a portfolio that now includes two majors, the uninspired TGL (which had below-network grade audio issues this week), and the Tour’s exclusive ESPN+ coverage. Showing more PGA Tour—a.k.a. real golf—seems like a natural fit.
And in another sign that the PGA Tour is looking to shake up its television package, CBS Sports president David Berson raved about new CEO Brian Rolapp and seemed open to efforts at reducing the schedule to create stronger fields. Given the need to generate more media rights revenue for the projected wealth forecast of the Tour’s player equity program, it still seems like a bold move to blow up the current deal and ask for more money while providing fewer hours of live golf. We’ll see.
Meanwhile, the LPGA Tour kicks off this week with most of its stars playing Lake Nona in Orlando, where miserable weather is expected for Saturday and Sunday’s final round (high of 45 degrees). And it’s a tough time to generate buzz given all of the off-course news surrounding the men’s game.
Peter Yagi Golf Books
In case you missed it, my trusted golf book seller friend Peter Yagi is having his annual post-Christmas sale where he’s offering 20% off with the purchase of 3 items or more through the end of January. Peter always has what I’m looking for, and his pricing is very fair given that he knows the market and focuses on first editions in excellent condition. He also has a good stock of my various books signed because, well, I just signed a few for him! Titles like The Captain, Alister MacKenzie’s Cypress Point Club, The Golden Age of Golf Design, Grounds for Golf, Lines of Charm, etc. are all available, according to Peter (even if you don’t see them listed in the catalog).
Just drop him a note at peteyagi1@gmail.com with questions or books you’re looking for since stuff comes and goes. Peter will let you know or can guide you to a great book in a category that excites you. He takes Venmo, Money Orders and Credit card payments via Paypal.

CBS Previews A Substantial 2026 Schedule
Rarely has minimal change sounded so refreshing.
The Farmers Insurance Open kicks off CBS Sports’ 2026 schedule. So the network convened a call to preview a new season where they appear ready to continue the tech-driven momentum of the last few years. Only in 2026, CBS will have a robust schedule thanks to picking up the PGA Tour playoffs. Lucky them!
In addition to The Masters and PGA Championship, CBS will broadcast 20 PGA Tour events and four LPGA Tour stops.
The new-look broadcast team debuts at Torrey Pines with Jim Nantz getting to anchor from on-site this year, former Masters champion Trevor Immelman returning as lead analyst, Colt Knost moving to the analyst role previously held by the now-retired Ian Baker-Finch, and Johnson Wagner making his CBS Sports debut as an on-course reporter. Frank Nobilo returns and will move up to the 17th hole that had been Baker-Finch’s territory. On-course, Wagner joins Dottie Pepper and Mark Immelman, while Amanda Balionis and Andrew Catalon also return.
The network suggested viewers will see a more robust use of social media and other outlets for “content” surrounding coverage. So if you know where to find CBS Sports Network…
Johnson Wagner, Shane Bacon and Patrick McDonald will convene each week for a golf preview show that will air on CBS Sports Network and be available on the
GOLF ON CBS YouTube channel. Wagner also will make regular content contributions to the network’s @GOLFonCBS platforms.GOLF ON CBS announcers also join CBS Sports HQ to provide round previews and recaps throughout the season.
The bells and whistles beefing up CBS Sports’ golf coverage in recent years return with more drone coverage during select weeks. There will also be CBS Sports’-driven “walk and talk” interviews, TrackMan swing data, and GOLFTEC OptiMotion swing analysis technology at signature events. More wind tracking and added drones for certain venues—with up to three some weeks—appear guaranteed for West Coast and major championship coverage.
“We’re always evolving with wind and other sources,” said producer Sellers Shy. “But we’re really excited about the package we have. I’m looking out at about 12 trucks right now, and everyone is excited.”
Coverage on CBS begins with Saturday’s third round of the Farmers.
Masters Odds And Some Prediction Market Silliness
With 70 days to the first tee shot, it’s time to take The Quad’s occasional look at Masters odds. As the domestic PGA Tour events kick off, it’s a two-man race at the moment: Scottie Scheffler is a 3-1 Masters favorite following his win at the American Express Championship. Defending champion Rory McIlroy is next at 7-1, while everyone else is at double-digits. That Collin Morikawa is at 30-1 is an astonishing thing given his recent play.
Then again, the lack of “oh yeah, he can win” names following the top three rows should have the PGA Tour worrying less about keeping Titleist executives happy and more about the developing “stars.”
Over at the what-could-go-wrong Polymarket, it seems “prediction” marketeers love Scheffler and a few players whose names required a Google translation assist. Брайсон Дешамбо seems to be Bryson DeChambeau, while Хон Рам is, well, Хон Рам. Not sure I’d put your hard-earned pennies down on Pam since the best translation I could get was Khan Ram, curiously close to Jon Rahm. But in a court of law I’m not sure you can confidently cash a ticket and claim Pam as Rahm.
Anyway, the future…
DCP Registration Opens, New Pace Bonuses Installed
Registration has opened for the 2027 Drive, Chip & Putt Championship and with it came news of a new pace policy at the National Finals.
You may recall—or not, since it seems like last year’s groundswell against Aimpoint putt-reading was fourteen years ago—the wee ones were Aimpointing way too much last year, prompting Chairman Fred Ridley to say something would be done.
“It’s interesting, but every phase of the competition has the same length chip and the same length putt, so it’s really not necessary to pace that off,” he said of the youngsters who made 2025’s finals. “They know how many yards that is. But nevertheless, that’s what they were doing. I think it’s safe to assume that next year at the Drive, Chip & Putt, you will see some sort of time limitations placed on the competition.”
According to the announcement for this year’s qualifying locations, a “pace of play bonus” will be implemented during the national finals where the kids can earn up to three additional points if they complete each shot during the competition in 40 seconds or less.
More trophy-for everybody-silliness.
I say just zap ‘em the little ones with a penalty stroke like they do on the PGA Tour! This’ll toughen ‘em up. Build that scar tissue. Induce some tears. Get ‘em ready for real life!
Oh, we kid the wee ones and the people who taught them that absurd-looking way to read a green.
Anyway, the 2026 qualifying schedule:
Local (May 2 to August)-- 353 host sites throughout all 50 states
-- Up to 3 juniors advance in each age/gender category from every venueSubregional (July and August)-- 64 host sites
-- 2 juniors advance in each age/gender category from every venueRegional (September and October)-- 10 host sites in 10 regions
-- 1 junior advances in each age/gender category from every venueNational Finals (April 4, 2027)-- 80 total participants at Augusta National Golf Club
Quotables
Brooks Koepka on going to LIV and now returning to the PGA Tour. “I don’t regret anything I do. I’ve learned a lot. I’ve always enjoyed the ride no matter where I’m at…you also learn from anything, anything you’re doing, so I have no regrets.”
Rory McIlroy on LIV after Brooks Koepka’s return. “It seems like some of those guys are maybe starting to realize they’re not getting everything they wanted out of going over there.”
Nelly Korda on the creation of a women’s TGL. “I have mixed feelings on it if I’m being very honest, and I’m surprised no other girls have, or no one’s really spoken out about it. I think it’s a huge and unbelievable miss that we’re not playing alongside the men. There’s no greater way to grow the game, and it would have been revolutionary. It would have been the first time, I think, that men and women are on the same playing field, playing for the same exact amount of money. But I also think it’s great that we are getting this opportunity, so that’s my mixed feelings.”
J.J. Spaun on how life has changed since winning the U.S. Open. “I get recognized a lot more than I have the last nine years, but it’s pretty cool. It’s kind of just a constant reminder of the success I’ve had and all the hard work that has paid off.”
Trevor Immelman on Scottie Scheffler’s consistency after the World No. 1 opened with a win at the AmEx. “He’s like the ocean. Like he doesn’t stop. He just keeps coming. That absolutely keeps his competition awake at night. A couple years ago you could say, ‘Oh well the putter is a little bit balky, and the stroke looks a little bit funky at times and he strikes it out of the heel and misses putts to the right’. But he’s gone ahead and turned that weakness into a strength over the last two seasons. If you go back to two years ago at the end of the season, he was 151st in putting. At the end of 2024, he was 70th. And at the end of 2025, he was 18th. So now you have a guy that is absolutely the best iron player in the game. If you combine distance and accuracy, he’s one of the best drivers of the ball. Oh, and now by the way he’s one of the best putters.”
Dottie Pepper on Scheffler. “We’ve come to this place with Scottie where he, in some ways a bit like Tiger and maybe even Jack did, forces people to do things out of their comfort zone. Take chances that they’re not normally accustomed to or comfortable taking because they know he’s not going to go away. Even when he doesn’t have his great stuff, he makes great decisions.”
This And That
The DP World Tour and Rolex announced an extension of their long-standing partnership dating to 1997. Rolex continues as Title Partner of the Rolex Series. The length of the contract extension was not revealed.
The European Tour Group announced that Gavin Green has received a three-month Anti-Doping Policy suspension after testing positive for a prohibited substance contained in an herbal supplement taken as a therapeutic treatment.
Fox Sports attempted to hype its upcoming LIV Golf coverage via a graphic featuring CEO Scott O’Neil at the top (!?), while misspelling Dustin Johnson, Martin Kaymer and Phil Mickelson’s names. The graphic was later deleted. The season-opening action begins next week in romantic Riyadh.
